result.topic_en: Euler argues that all forces acting on the clamped portion Aa of the elastic lamina reduce to two forces at A and a. He then reduces the vibration problem to an equilibrium problem by applying the elementary forces YV = K dx/(2bk) (ddy/dt^2) in the contrary direction.

items.quote:
vnicam vim verbi gratia
in puncto A applicatam, quantumuis fuerit magna,
nequaquam inflexioni refiftere poffe
items.english: A single force applied, for example, at point A, however large it may be, can by no means resist the bending.

items.quote:
omnes vires, quibus lamina noftra
actu follicitatur, femper reduci poffe ad binas vires
in punctis A et $a$ applicatas
items.english: All forces by which our lamina is actually acted upon can always be reduced to two forces applied at the points A and a.

items.quote:
verum
ipfa demum folutio nobis has vires declarabit, atque
tum manifeftum fiet quantas vires murus feu paries
a portione infixa A$a$ quouis momento fuftineat
items.english: But the solution itself will finally reveal these forces to us, and then it will become clear what forces the wall sustains at any moment from the embedded portion Aa.

items.quote:
Tota ergo quaeftio huc redit, quomodo
vires illae elementares $YV = \frac{K\,dx}{2bk}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right)$ comparatae
effe debeant, vt binis illis viribus in A et $a$ appli-
candis etiamfi ignotis aequiualeant
items.english: The whole question therefore comes down to this: how must those elementary forces YV = K dx/(2bk) (ddy/dt^2) be constituted so that they are equivalent to the two forces to be applied at A and a, even though these are unknown?

items.quote:
ficque hoc modo tota quaeftio ad inueftigationem
ftatus aequilibrii reducitur, ita vt nunc non amplius
ipfe motus in confiderationem veniat
items.english: In this way the whole question is reduced to the investigation of a state of equilibrium, so that the motion itself no longer needs to be considered.
